title: TCHP · subcutaneous trastuzumab

agents.name: Docetaxel
agents.explanation: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected.
agents.watch: Take prescribed steroid premedication. Report fever, lasting numbness, swelling, sore nails or infusion symptoms.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and sepsis
Hair loss, mouth soreness and fatigue

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin creates links in DNA, making it harder for cells to copy and repair their genetic instructions. Its dose depends on kidney function as well as the intended regimen.
agents.watch: Keep blood-test appointments. Fever, unusual bleeding, repeated vomiting or infusion symptoms need prompt advice.
risks: Low blood counts, infection and bleeding
Allergic reaction, sometimes after previous exposure

agents.name: Trastuzumab
agents.explanation: Trastuzumab binds to the HER2 protein on cells and helps reduce HER2-driven growth and recruit immune activity. HER2 testing identifies the cancers for which this approach is used.
agents.watch: Keep echo appointments throughout HER2 treatment. Report breathlessness, swelling, palpitations or a reaction; chemotherapy side effects are tracked separately.

agents.name: Pertuzumab
agents.mechanism: Blocks HER2 pairing with other receptors
agents.explanation: Pertuzumab binds a different area of HER2 from trastuzumab. It limits receptor pairing, so the two antibodies act together at different points on the same growth pathway.
agents.watch: Report diarrhoea early, especially with poor fluid intake. Keep cardiac checks and report infusion symptoms immediately.

purpose: This treatment is part of a plan to reduce the chance of breast cancer returning.
schedule_summary: Six 21-day cycles before surgery: IV pertuzumab, fixed-dose trastuzumab under the skin, IV docetaxel and IV carboplatin. Surgery and pathology guide the postoperative HER2 plan. This is not the combined Phesgo injection.

phases_title: The phases and how they connect
phases_note: Each phase has its own medicines, checks and supportive prescription. A change of phase does not restart the cardiac monitoring clock.
timeline_note: These broad symptom bands are educational possibilities, not measured risk curves. Infusion days are the planned schedule; delays require a new clinical plan.
safety_note: Fever, shivers, sudden illness, severe breathing changes or chest pain need prompt assessment on any day.
teachback: Which phase are you in, what changes next, and who is arranging and reviewing your next blood test, echo or scan?
consent_support: Discuss treatment aim, alternatives, uncertainty, fertility, contraception, access, phase changes, serious and lasting risks, supportive medicines and the urgent contact plan.
urgent_extra: Report new breathing symptoms, severe diarrhoea, inability to drink, painful swollen limbs, unusual bleeding, or worsening numbness. Tell staff immediately about infusion-site pain or an allergic reaction.

support.title: The correct phase prescription
support.text: Carboplatin AUC 6 uses the NCCP high-risk carboplatin row.

support.title: Premedicines and growth factors
support.text: Docetaxel dexamethasone is taken for three days starting the day before treatment. Ask the team to reconcile this with antiemetic steroids.

support.title: Tests and appointments
support.text: The team should name the booking owner, due window and person reviewing each required test. Tell them if an expected appointment has not arrived.

support.title: After chemotherapy
support.text: HER2-only continuation has its own minimal-emetic-risk plan; do not automatically continue chemotherapy steroids, antiemetics or growth factors.

questions.a: Six 21-day cycles before surgery: IV pertuzumab, fixed-dose trastuzumab under the skin, IV docetaxel and IV carboplatin. Surgery and pathology guide the postoperative HER2 plan. This is not the combined Phesgo injection.

Baseline before HER2 treatment; repeat every 12 weeks during treatment. Repeat at completion; 4–8-week checks may be needed with impairment. Count 12 weeks from first HER2 treatment (after AC where applicable): around weekly antibody dose 13 or q21-day cycle 5. Preserve elapsed time across later phase / route changes and delays.

questions.q: Where do surgery and radiotherapy fit?
questions.a: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy precedes surgery. Pathology determines postoperative systemic therapy; radiotherapy follows the surgical / systemic plan and can overlap HER2 treatment when agreed.

questions.q: Do I need routine CT scans or tumour markers?
questions.a: Assess the breast / nodes before treatment and response during the neoadjuvant course to guide surgery; modality and interval follow the MDT plan. New symptoms can require earlier assessment. Later asymptomatic early-breast surveillance is different from metastatic CT monitoring. After local treatment: annual mammography of remaining breast tissue; additional imaging when indicated.

questions.q: Does a port mean a pump at home?
questions.a: No. This regimen has no routine take-home infusion pump. A port is an access device; the team removes the needle after the visit when appropriate and arranges device removal separately.

evidence.title: TRYPHAENA · neoadjuvant dual HER2 blockade
evidence.intro: Evidence is specific to the population, medicines and schedule studied.
evidence.population: Phase II neoadjuvant HER2-positive early breast cancer cardiac-safety study with several chemotherapy backbones.
evidence.interpretation: Supports the studied neoadjuvant combination and cardiac-safety context. It does not directly test this SC trastuzumab formulation or establish survival equivalence across backbones.

items.text: FBC, renal and liver profile before each cycle. Weekly-day checks follow the active regimen and local delivery policy.

items.text: Baseline before HER2 treatment; repeat every 12 weeks during treatment. Repeat at completion; 4–8-week checks may be needed with impairment. EMA: cardiac checks every 6 months after trastuzumab ends until 24 months; after anthracyclines in early disease, yearly to 5 years from the last trastuzumab dose or longer if function falls.

chapters.title: Surgery, radiation and longer treatment
chapters.intro: The whole pathway may extend beyond chemotherapy.

items.title: Local treatment
items.text: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy precedes surgery. Pathology determines postoperative systemic therapy; radiotherapy follows the surgical / systemic plan and can overlap HER2 treatment when agreed.

items.title: Endocrine and bone health
items.text: If hormone-receptor-positive disease leads to an aromatase inhibitor / ovarian suppression, assess baseline DEXA and fracture risk. Repeat according to risk, results and the endocrine plan; this is not a universal chemotherapy test.

items.title: Treatment selection
items.text: Oncotype / genomic scoring is not automatically inferred from this regimen. Where relevant, the MDT considers receptor status, stage, menopausal status and validated assay eligibility.

chronology_notes.text: The chart explains the pattern. Your team books actual appointments and reviews results.

chronology_notes.title: Phase changes
chronology_notes.text: Supportive medicines and symptom expectations change when chemotherapy stops. HER2-only treatment does not automatically inherit chemotherapy premedicines.

chronology_notes.title: Treatment delays
chronology_notes.text: A delayed dose does not automatically delay an echo or other test that is already due.

logistics.title: Your practical treatment plan
logistics.intro: Six 21-day cycles before surgery: IV pertuzumab, fixed-dose trastuzumab under the skin, IV docetaxel and IV carboplatin. Surgery and pathology guide the postoperative HER2 plan. This is not the combined Phesgo injection.

steps.title: Before the first visit
steps.text: Blood tests, relevant cardiac assessment, medicines review, fertility discussion and the consent conversation come first.

steps.title: Plan venous access
steps.text: A cannula, PICC or implanted port may be used. If a port is chosen, a trained team inserts it in a separate procedure with local anaesthetic and sometimes sedation; the team explains fasting, blood-thinner and wound instructions.

steps.title: Infusion day
steps.text: IV pertuzumab and chemotherapy still require venous access. Trastuzumab 600 mg is a separate thigh injection; this is not Phesgo. Staff check the line, give prescribed premedicines and treatment, and observe for reactions. Tell them immediately about burning, pain, rash or breathlessness.

steps.title: Home and next review
steps.text: This regimen does not routinely need a take-home infusion pump. Staff disconnect the infusion; a port is de-accessed when appropriate. Keep line-care and next-visit instructions.

details.title: Port insertion and removal
details.text: The line team explains placement, dressing care and when normal activities can resume. A port is accessed with a special needle during treatment. Removal of the implanted device is a separate planned procedure when no longer needed; do not remove or adjust it yourself.

details.title: PICC care and urgent line symptoms
details.text: A PICC usually needs regular dressing and flushing appointments even between treatments. Fever, redness, swelling, pain, leakage or damage requires prompt advice. Your hospital supplies the exact care instructions.

details.title: Visit time and transport
details.text: First visits can take longer because of loading doses, premedicines and observation. Ask the unit about expected time, transport and any escort needed after sedation or line insertion.

details.title: Phase-specific visit pattern
details.text: Infusion and observation times differ by drug and first versus later doses; the unit confirms the full visit duration, including blood review and preparation.
